---
title: "mermaid source that looks like markdown, then ojs"
format: html
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - ["pre.mermaid.mermaid-js", "div[id^=\"ojs-cell-\"]"]
        - []
      ensureHtmlElementCount:
        - selectors: ["pre.mermaid.mermaid-js"]
          counts: [2]
---

Each `mermaid` cell below is emitted verbatim into the intermediate markdown,
inside a raw HTML block. If anything in the diagram source ends that block early,
the rest of the document is misread, and the `ojs` cell at the end is not
compiled.

The first diagram carries Mermaid's own `---` front matter to set `config`. Its
closing `---` used to be read as the start of a YAML front matter block that
swallowed everything after it.

```{mermaid}
---
config:
    look: handDrawn
---
graph LR
    A --> B
```

The second diagram uses Mermaid markdown strings. A label with a single backtick
comes first, then a line that starts with three backticks. The raw block fence
must be longer than the longest backtick run, not the first one, or that line
closes the block.

````{mermaid}
graph LR
A["`a tick label`"] --> B["`two
```
lines`"]
````

```{ojs}
//| echo: true
x = 2
x ** 5
```
